8ae77b40bf44aff69e51e6a6e5111a288e3877d3.summary: Introductory page of a Chinese-language documentation series on Cobalt Strike 4.1, a penetration-testing and adversary-simulation tool. It outlines the series in three parts: basic use, advanced topics such as C2 configuration and proxying, and internals. It describes no threat actor, campaign, malware incident or vulnerability, so it is not a threat report.
hedges: The author says they are not a specialist in Cobalt Strike and the notes are a spare-time record.
The author says updates are irregular and errors may be present, and asks readers to point them out.
The page says it provides no finished tools, only ideas or reference material.
The page says it will not cover antivirus bypass techniques, which are planned for a separate document.

8ae7243e78d70618e1eff845156b8d689095e493.summary: BlackBerry's Research and Intelligence Team describes BHunt, a .NET crypto-stealer. Bitdefender first reported it, with a dropper likely packaged with KMS cracking utilities. BHunt looks for crypto wallet files, steals browser passwords, monitors the clipboard for 12 or 13 word recovery phrases, and checks whether a system suits a crypto miner (XMRig). It uses commercial packers (VMProtect, Themida), autorun registry persistence, and legitimate NirSoft WebBrowserPassView. Some payload retrieval used Pastebin links that are no longer hosted.

hedges: The dropper was likely packaged with Key Management Service (KMS) cracking utilities, per the report's description of the initial infection.
The Pastebin links are no longer hosted, so the downloaded data could not be confirmed.
The purpose of the Chaos_crew function appears to be evaluating a system's suitability for installing a crypto miner.
The purpose of the Copier binary is a mystery; the report believes it is part of the same malware campaign.
The miner file is believed to be XMRig.
